# Shared Packages

`packages/core` (`@statglass/core`, imported as `@core/*`) is shared by the desktop app and
the iPhone app. The test for anything shared, from RFC `plan/rfc-ios-app.md` 4.6: "If the
desktop changes this, should the phone change too, without anyone deciding?" Yes means
shared; "it depends" means per platform.

## What is shared

Formatters, chart math, live and history state, host clock, series keys, query keys,
remote errors, the mock transport with its scenarios and fixtures, generated types, widget
models, popover composition (card order, subscribed series, density) and tokens. Rendered
elements, card chrome, layout, spacing, interaction, motion implementation, navigation and
platform hooks are per platform.

## Guards

1. Pull, never push: code moves into `packages/` in the same change that adds its second consumer; no bulk moves of `src/app/hooks` or `src/app/widgets`, and a widget the phone never renders keeps its logic in the desktop app.
2. No platform code: `packages/core` never imports `react`, `react-dom`, `react-native`, `expo`, `expo-*`, `@tauri-apps/*`, `@steamfield/ui` or `@desktop/*`, and never uses `window`, `document` or `navigator`; Biome and the write hook reject it.
3. Fork instead of flagging: when a shared model needs an option only one platform uses, that platform copies the model and the copy is listed in `packages/core/README.md`; never add a platform parameter.
4. Tested once, rendered twice: model tests assert view models from the shared fixtures, and each app's gallery renders the same fixtures; pixel comparison stays within each platform.
5. Every shared change is checked by both apps: run `bun run check` and `make mobile-check` for any change under `packages/`, as Linux CI does.
6. The desktop's performance gates hold: extracting a model is a pure refactor, and render-count tests, `make e2e-perf` and the idle-CPU budget stay green.
7. Each app pins its own React; core declares no `react` dependency, and a shared package that needs one takes it as a peer.

## Widget models

- A model is a pure function from the widget's existing props type, plus measurable inputs (width, density), to a view model of token names, final strings and final geometry.
- Models take measurable inputs, never a platform enum, so neither app's needs leak into the other's output.
- Keep models allocation-light on the 1 Hz path: no per-tick closures, maps or sorts the desktop component did not already do.
- The desktop component keeps its name and props, so routes do not change; the phone twin takes the same props type.
- Accessibility labels and value text come from the model, so both apps announce the same words.
- Extract one widget at a time with the `widget-model` skill.
